newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Indigo shakeup aimed at raising sales.
newsitem.headline: Indigo shakeup aimed at raising sales.

text.p: Israel's Indigo NV, coming off a string of heavy losses, said on Monday it had appointed a new top sales executive and made other managerial changes.

Chairman Benny Landa said the appointment of George Carlisle as president of Indigo America, the company's U.S. marketing unit, was aimed at raising the company's flagging sales of digital offset printing equipment.
Carlisle served as president of the U.S. marketing unit of Scitex Corp, another Israeli company, from 1986 to 1995.
"With George Carlisle at the helm, we are now ready to embark on a major sales and marketing thrust in North America," Landa said in a letter to customers.

Landa said the outgoing president, Frank Steenburgh, was leaving the company along with corporate president Wayland Hicks, whose job was made redundant by the formation of a committee of executives who will report directly to the chairman.
The Dutch-registered company, which operates primarily out of Israel, has faced difficulties selling its innovative digital-printing technology.

Indigo pioneered digital offset printing, but it reported a loss of $1.08 a share in the first nine months of 1996, compared with a $0.42 a share loss in the year-earlier period. Revenues slumped to $80.1 million from $128.6 million a year earlier.
